Estimate a network

Source: R/build_network.R, R/summary_network.R
build_network.Rd

build_network() estimates a network from sequences, an event log, one-hot codes or numeric variables, with the estimator named by method, and returns a netobject: the object every other Nestimate verb reads (bootstrap, permutation, centrality, clustering, plotting). Each method's arguments are on its own page, named under method; they are given here by name, as in build_network(df, method = "relative", actor = "id").

Column roles are declared, never read from names or values, and input that fits none of the readings raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. The weights are point estimates: see how far they move under resampling with bootstrap_network(), and compare groups with permutation().

Usage

build_network(
  data,
  method,
  ...,
  group = NULL,
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  labels = NULL,
  inherit = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
print(x, n = 10L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_ml'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
summary(object, combined = TRUE, format = c("long", "wide"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.netobject'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.netobject_group'
x[i, j, ...]

# S3 method for class 'summary.netobject_group'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

The data the method reads (see its page), or a fitted clustering (net_clustering, net_mmm), to build one network per cluster with the clustering's method. Per-cluster "latency" networks are not available (a clustering keeps the sequences, not the event times): name another method, or the error has class nestimate_latency_clusters.

method

The estimator. Each has its own page with its arguments:

Sequences and event logs
"relative"transition network analysis (TNA)see build_tna() for details
"frequency"frequency transition network analysis (FTNA)see build_ftna() for details
"attention"attention transition network analysis (ATNA)see build_atna() for details
"co_occurrence"co-occurrence network analysis (CNA)see build_cna() for details
"ngram"n-gram transition network analysissee build_ngram() for details
"gap"gap transition network analysissee build_gap() for details
"reverse"reverse (reply) transition network analysissee build_reverse() for details
Message logs
"latency"latency network analysissee build_latency() for details
One-hot codes
"wtna"window transition network analysis (WTNA)see build_wtna() for details
"wtna_cooccurrence"window co-occurrence network analysissee wtna() for details
Numeric variables
"cor"correlation networksee build_cor() for details
"pcor"partial correlation networksee build_pcor() for details
"glasso"EBIC graphical lasso networksee build_glasso() for details
"ising"Ising modelsee build_ising() for details
"mgm"mixed graphical model (MGM)see build_mgm() for details

The other names list_estimators() shows ("tna", "ftna", "atna", "cna", ...) also work, and an estimator added with register_estimator() is called by its name. Required, except for a fitted clustering, whose own method is used.

...

The method's arguments, by name, as listed on its page, such as actor, action, start or lambda. For the print() and summary() methods: ignored.

group

A column to split the data by: one network per value, returned as a netobject_group. Default NULL.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" rescales the weights to run from 0 to 1, over every cell for the transition methods (tna's rule, so with no zero cell the smallest weight becomes 0) and over the non-zero weights, into (0, 1], for the other methods, "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1; an undirected network whose matrix it makes asymmetric becomes directed, so both of a pair's values are kept as edges. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none).

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names. Default NULL.

inherit

Only when data is a fitted clustering (net_clustering or net_mmm) of a network: whether the per-cluster networks also take that network's threshold, scaling and estimator settings. FALSE (default) builds them with its method and the arguments given here; TRUE uses its settings for any not given here, when the clusters are built with its method. The relative networks of a net_mmm are the fitted chains, which take only its threshold and scaling.

x

For the print() methods: a netobject, netobject_group or netobject_ml, or the result of summary() on one.

n

For print() of a netobject: the number of edges listed, strongest first, self-loops included. Default 10; Inf lists them all, as does extract_edges() with include_self = TRUE; extract_transition_matrix() the weight matrix and extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.

digits

For print() of a netobject_group: decimal places of the weight range. Default 3.

object

For summary(): a netobject or netobject_group.

combined

For summary() of a netobject_group: TRUE (default) joins the groups' metrics into one data frame; FALSE returns a named list of the per-group tables.

format

For summary() of a netobject_group with combined = TRUE: "long" (default), one row per metric and group (metric, group, value), or "wide", one row per metric with a column per group. Both print as a metric-by-group grid.

i, j

For [ on a grouped summary: rows and columns, as for a data frame. A subset is a plain data frame.

Value

A netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network")). Print it for an overview; extract_edges() gives one row per edge, extract_transition_matrix() and extract_initial_probs() the weights and initial-state probabilities, and cograph::splot() draws it. summary() returns the descriptive metrics, one row per metric (a netobject_group gives one row per metric and group, with a group column). The print() methods return their input invisibly. The netobject's fields:

data

The state columns of the cleaned input data, as a data frame.

metadata

Data frame of the non-state columns of the cleaned input (and, for long input, the per-sequence metadata), or NULL.

weights

The estimated network weight matrix.

nodes

Data frame with columns id, label, name, x, y.

edges

Data frame of non-zero edges with integer from/to (node IDs) and numeric weight.

directed

Logical. Whether the network is directed.

method

The resolved method name.

params

The params list used (for reproducibility).

scaling

The scaling applied (or NULL).

threshold

The threshold applied.

n_nodes

Number of nodes.

n_edges

Number of non-zero edges.

level

Decomposition level used, or NULL; for mgm built without a decomposition, the category count of each variable.

build_args

The resolved column/format arguments (actor, action, time, session, order, codes, format, window_size, mode) used for this build.

meta

List with source, layout, and tna metadata (cograph-compatible).

node_groups

Node groupings data frame, or NULL.

predictability

Named numeric vector of R-squared predictability values per node, for cor, pcor and glasso when predictability = TRUE; NULL otherwise.

The estimator's own results are kept beside these fields, depending on the method: for example frequency_matrix and initial for relative, frequency, ngram, gap and reverse (only initial for attention, neither for co_occurrence), cor_matrix and the sample size n for cor, pcor and glasso, precision_matrix for pcor and glasso, and lambda_selected for glasso. A latency network keeps initial, n_replies and median_latency (matrices laid out as the weights), latency_cap_seconds (the resolved global cap, also in params), latency_unit_caps (the per-unit caps of a non-global latency_scope, named by unit, also in params) and latency_time, the event times in seconds (and, for the "actor" and "session" scopes, each sequence's unit), one row per row of data.

With level = "both", the result is a netobject_ml holding the between-person and within-person networks (between and within, each a netobject) and the method. level = "between" or "within" returns a single netobject estimated on the decomposed data.

With group, or when data is a net_clustering or net_mmm object, the result is a netobject_group: a named list of netobjects, one per group, that records the grouping column in its group_col attribute.

Methods

Printing a netobject shows the kind of network, the range of its weights (with the numbers of positive and negative edges for cor, pcor, glasso and ising, the mean weight otherwise), the weight matrix under the node labels, the initial probabilities and the predictability values when present, the sample size for cor, pcor, glasso and ising, the tuning values of glasso and ising, and any scaling or threshold. Printing a netobject_group gives a header naming its source (a clustering from build_network() on a net_clustering or net_mmm fit, or cluster_network(), or a plain split by the grouping column) and one row per group with its node and edge counts and weight range; when the groups are clusters, it also shows the number and share of sequences in each, in the layout of the build_clusters() and build_mmm() prints. A netobject_ml prints the node, edge and sample counts of its between- and within-person networks.

summary() gives the descriptive metrics tna::summary.tna() reports: node and edge counts, density, mean shortest-path distance, the mean and SD of out- and in-strength, the mean and SD of out-degree, out- and in-degree centralisation (Freeman) and reciprocity. A self-loop counts as an edge, and an undirected edge is counted once. Density divides the edge count, self-loops included, by the n(n - 1) off-diagonal pairs (n(n - 1) / 2 when undirected), as tna::summary.tna() and igraph::edge_density(loops = FALSE) do, and is capped at 1. Strengths sum absolute weights. Distances take each edge's absolute weight as its length, not its inverse, and pairs with no path between them are left out of the mean. Degree centralisation ignores self-loops, and reciprocity is the share of off-diagonal edges whose reverse is also present (1 for an undirected network). Mean distance and reciprocity are NaN when no pair qualifies. Printing a summary shows the counts as integers and the other metrics to four significant digits.

References

Saqr, M., López-Pernas, S., Törmänen, T., Kaliisa, R., Misiejuk, K., & Tikka, S. (2025). Transition network analysis: A novel framework for modeling, visualizing, and identifying the temporal patterns of learners and learning processes. In Proceedings of the 15th International Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK25). ACM. doi:10.1145/3706468.3706513

See also

list_estimators() and register_estimator() for the estimator registry; bootstrap_network(), permutation() and net_centrality() for what to do with the network.

Examples

build_network(trajectories, method = "relative")
#> Transition Network (relative probabilities) [directed]
#>   Weights: [0.035, 0.698]  |  mean: 0.333
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (9 of 9):
#>    from       to         weight
#>    Active     Active     0.698 
#>    Average    Average    0.610 
#>    Disengaged Disengaged 0.483 
#>    Disengaged Average    0.397 
#>    Active     Average    0.267 
#>    Average    Active     0.204 
#>    Average    Disengaged 0.186 
#>    Disengaged Active     0.120 
#>    Active     Disengaged 0.035  
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix;
#>   extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.
build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "relative", actor = "Actor",
              action = "Action", time = "Time", group = "Course")
#> Group Networks (3 groups, group_col: Course)
#> 
#>   Group  Nodes  Edges  Weights
#>   A      9      76     [0.002, 0.581]
#>   B      9      76     [0.000, 0.479]
#>   C      9      74     [0.001, 0.440]
build_network(trajectories, method = "attention", lambda = 2)
#> Attention Network (decay-weighted transitions) [directed]
#>   Weights: [44.056, 608.921]  |  mean: 263.021
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (9 of 9):
#>    from       to         weight 
#>    Average    Average    608.921

#>    Average    Active     227.679

#>    Disengaged Active      57.105
#>    Active     Disengaged  44.056 
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix;
#>   extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.
build_network(srl_strategies, method = "glasso", gamma = 0.25)
